chapter: The Paradise and life in Queens
title: Drugs around the musicians and why he stayed away
summary: Friends used heroin to concentrate on music; he understood but declined, and helped when he could.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: You mentioned, a few minutes back, the issue of drug use and I wonder what the history of that is, in your own experience...people that you knew who were affected by that, your own...

Well, I'll tell you something. I never ... I won't mention any names ... they tried to romance me into this, but I just didn't... I understood what it was, they wanted to get a little peace of mind so they could concentrate on music, you know, and with so much goin' on, they wanted to dedicate their-self and it seems that heroin would isolate a person so they could concentrate, wholly, on

what they were doin' and they wouldn't have no distractions. But the price that had to be paid, you had to have a job and, you know, they go to sleep and get to the point where you start stealin' and all kind of things, you know, which was against the grain. But when you get this craving in your blood stream, you know, it's a drug, you see. And I felt sorry for the people, you know, we were friends. But I understood what it was, you see what I mean, and it was all around me all the the time. Yeah. But I understood what it was, the guys wanted to get so they could concentrate more on what they were doin', which I could understand. You know, this takes a lot of understanding, but I understood it. So I didn't...
Would people actually present that to you as a reason for trying it, a musical reason?
No, they were very nice to me, 'cause everybody liked me and they never would come out and say, "Nick, come on." They never

did get to that point. Because they could tell, you know, the guys were, most of them, so gifted, you know what I mean. And smart, you know, they knew, you know, "Don't approach Nick with that, 'cause he ain't goin' for it." You know, the way I conducted myself. But I didn't disrespect anyone because of that. And if I could help, I helped, you know, spiritually and financially and etcetera, etcetera. So I don't like to talk about things like that.
